chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Uqda said to us: Ahmad ibn Yusuf ibn Ya'qub, Abu al-Hasan al-Ja'fi, narrated to me from his book, saying: Isma'il ibn Mihran narrated to us from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from his father, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdillah said:

There must be a tribulation before the appearance of al-Qa'im, during which people will hunger, and severe fear of killing will befall them, and there will be loss of wealth, lives, and fruits; for that is clearly stated in the Book of Allah.
And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits; but give good tidings to the patient.

key_terms.الْقَائِم: The Awaited One, referring to Imam al-Mahdi

ai.seo_question: What are the signs of hunger and loss before the appearance of al-Qa'im according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies a specific year of severe tribulation preceding the appearance of al-Qa'im, characterized by hunger, fear, and loss of wealth, lives, and produce. He explicitly links this to Quran 2:155, emphasizing that these trials are divinely ordained and clearly mentioned in the Scripture. This narration underscores the Shia belief in a transitional period of hardship that purifies the believers before the establishment of global justice.
